text.p: Bonds closed little changed on Friday as the market awaited the French audit of state finances which is due to be released on Monday, traders said.
Traders said that the spread should remain comfortably around 70 basis points to the Bund where it appears to have stabilised in recent sessions.
"The 10 years took advantage of the falls (in prices) of foreign markets to take some profit. But at the close, there was good support and they recovered from lows," said one trader.
It was even possible that the spread with the Bunds could narrow slightly, some traders said.

The market was expecting France to report it was heading for a state deficit of 3.5 percent of GDP in 1997 but that it would at the same time announce convincing measures to reduce the budget gap, traders said.
"The audit will be decisive for the market trend. But nobody is unduly worried as a deficit of around 3.5 percent is expected but together with measures to control it," said one trader.
With support seeming strong at around the 70 basis point spread level, the 10 years could even narrow the gap towards 65 basis points on the above scenario, the trader added.
